threshold: 0 false failures of `scaling_ratio < 2.5` on an O(1) implementation whose per-fill cost falls below half a clock tick (measured tick 15.625 ms, i.e. below ~7.8 µs/fill); the 250 µs ceilings and the 2.5 ratio must stay unchanged
measurement: At 2e7f51b the benchmark times its two loops with time.process_time(); on this Windows interpreter the clock advances in a single 15.625 ms step (2 distinct values in 20,000 calls). Quantizing an O(1) implementation costing 5 µs/fill gives 1,000 fills = 0.0 µs/fill (below half a tick) and 4,000 fills = 3.91 µs/fill, so scaling_ratio = 3.91 ≥ 2.5 and the test fails on a faster implementation while the true ratio is 1.0. At the current cost (46.9 µs/fill at 1k, 46.9-66.4 at 4k, ratio 0.75-1.42 over five repetitions) the window is not reached, so this is latent. The defect is Windows-bound: on a host with a nanosecond process_time the same workload measures near 1.0, and probe_n173 asserts that branch separately. Test-only: no gate assertion is weakened, a false failure is still fail-closed.
